cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Urban – relating to a town or city.

p.em: Example: We need to build more green parks in urban areas.

cosy-blockquote.p: Protect – to keep someone or something safe from harm or danger.

p.em: Example: We must protect bees because they help grow our food.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hive – a container or box where bees live and make honey.

p.em: Example: The beekeeper opened the wooden hive very carefully.

cosy-blockquote.p: Environment – the natural world, including the air, water, land, and plants.

p.em: Example: City pollution is very bad for the environment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Community – a group of people living in the same place or having a common interest.

p.em: Example: Our local community works together to clean the park.

cosy-blockquote.p: Wild – living or growing in nature; not kept or controlled by humans.

p.em: Example: We can see beautiful wild animals in the national forest.

cosy-blockquote.p: Beekeeper – a person who owns and takes care of bees.

p.em: Example: The beekeeper wears a white protective suit to avoid stings.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hobby – an activity that you do for pleasure when you are not working.

p.em: Example: My favorite hobby is taking photos of nature.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plant – a living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.

p.em: Example: I bought a small green plant for my living room.

cosy-blockquote.p: Useful – helping you to do or achieve what you want; having a practical use.

p.em: Example: A dictionary is a very useful tool for language students.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How usually do you find green parks in your crowded urban area, and what plants grow there?
★ Do you prefer living in highly urban cities or quiet, rural villages?

Why can we always protect bees from city pollution by planting flowers on balconies?
★ Do you buy organic products to protect the local environment?

Why does a beekeeper sometimes place a wooden hive on a tall building roof?
★ Have you ever stood near a real hive with active bees?

How does city traffic noise usually affect the delicate natural environment?
★ Do you try to save water to help protect our environment?

How can a local community often build a green garden together in their neighborhood?
★ Are you active in your local neighborhood community?

Why do we sometimes find beautiful, wild flowers growing between concrete blocks?
★ When was the last time you walked in a wild, untouched forest?

What tools does a modern beekeeper always use when working in the apiary?
★ Would you like to try the work of a beekeeper for one day?

Is growing green plants on windowsills usually a relaxing hobby for city residents?
★ What is your favorite outdoor hobby?

Why do people sometimes keep a delicate plant on their busy office desk?
★ Do you prefer green houseplants or colorful flowers in your room?

Why are insects like honey bees always incredibly useful for our city's food supply?
★ What is the most useful tips you have learned about saving energy?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, every urban school will always have a honey hive on its roof.
★ Would you support having a bee hive at your local school?

Governments will sometimes pay citizens to protect rare wild flowers on balconies.
★ Would you grow more flowers if the government paid you to protect them?

Humans will never destroy the natural environment completely to live in underground cities.
★ Would you want to live in a clean virtual city if the real environment became too polluted?

Every local community will usually grow its own organic food in vertical gardens.
★ Do you think vertical gardens are a useful way to grow food in cities?

Being a beekeeper will often become the most fashionable outdoor hobby for young adults.
★ Would you tell your friends if your new hobby was keeping bees?

We will sometimes build gigantic artificial trees to help clean the urban air.
★ Do you think artificial trees are useful or a waste of money?

A robotic plant will always clean the dust inside our apartments.
★ Would you buy a robotic plant or a real green fern?

City laws will usually make it illegal to use chemical sprays to save wild insects.
★ Do you actively avoid chemical sprays in your household?

Every citizen will sometimes have to help their community in local parks.
★ Would you enjoy spending a weekend cleaning parks with your neighbors?

A tiny tracking chip will usually be placed on queen bees to protect hives.
★ Do you think tracking queen bees is useful for science?

ul.li: Incorrect: The bee have beautiful wings. → Correct: The bee has beautiful wings. ((Subject-verb agreement: 'The bee' is singular, use 'has'.))
Incorrect: I saw a bee on yesterday. → Correct: I saw a bee yesterday. ((Time adverb: do not use the preposition 'on' before 'yesterday'.))
Incorrect: He is afraid to bees. → Correct: He is afraid of bees. ((Preposition check: the adjective 'afraid' is followed by the preposition 'of'.))
